Callers treat the return uniformly: Hubspot accesses `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM access `tokenInfo.data.error`, both of which are undefined/throw on a raw fetch Response, breaking token refresh in credential-sync mode.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` Response when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple callers still assume the return value is an SDK/axios result or token object: Hubspot assigns it to `HubspotToken` (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts), Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM treat it like an axios response and access `.data.error` (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts). A `fetch` Response has no `.data`, and it’s not a token object, so in sync mode these refresh paths will break and can leave credentials stale.
